title: Smallest All-Ones Multiple
summary: Given a positive integer k, determine the least number of digits in an integer n, which is a multiple of k and composed entirely of the digit 1.
statement: Given a positive integer k, determine the least number of digits in an integer n, which is a multiple of k and composed entirely of the digit 1. If no such n exists, return -1.
constraints: The sought positive integer contains only decimal digit one.
Return its digit count, or -1 when no such multiple exists.
reference_solution:
def smallest_all_ones_multiple_length(k):
    if k%2==0 or k%5==0:return -1
    remainder=0
    for length in range(1,k+1):
        remainder=(remainder*10+1)%k
        if remainder==0:return length
    return -1
hints: Building the integer itself is unnecessary; only its remainder modulo k matters.
Append a one with remainder=(remainder·10+1) mod k.
At most k nonzero remainders can occur before repetition; return when zero appears.
A repunit exists exactly when k has no factor two or five, and the finite remainder sequence must then reach zero.
editorial: A repunit exists exactly when k has no factor two or five, and the finite remainder sequence must then reach zero.

tests.explanation: The first divisible repunit is 111, which has three digits.
111111 is divisible by seven, while every shorter repunit is not.
